summary: Registers the application/pkix-attr-cert MIME media type, used to carry a single attribute certificate as defined in RFC 5755. It is informational.

eli5.summary: It gives a label for an envelope that holds one special permission card, so programs know what is inside.

subtitle: The registered media type for sending a single attribute certificate.

tldr.problem: Attribute certificates had no registered MIME media type, unlike public key certificates and CRLs, which RFC 2585 covers.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers application/pkix-attr-cert with IANA for a single attribute certificate as defined in RFC 5755.
tldr.outcome: Attribute certificates can be fetched and transferred with a labeled media type, for example over HTTP; the file extension is .ac.

today: RFC 5877 is an Informational RFC published in May 2010. No later RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Why a New Media Type
sections.content:
RFC 2585 defines MIME media types for public key certificates and certificate revocation lists. RFC 5877 adds one for attribute certificates as defined in RFC 5755.

Attribute certificates are ASN.1 encoded. RFC 5755 says which parts must use DER and which may use BER. Since DER is a proper subset of BER, BER decoding all parts of a properly constructed attribute certificate will succeed.
sections.eli5: Some certificates already had labels for their envelopes. The permission-card certificate was missing one, so this note adds it.

sections.title: The Registration
sections.content:
The type name is application and the subtype name is pkix-attr-cert. There are no required or optional parameters, and the encoding is binary. The file extension is .ac, and there is no magic number. The intended usage is COMMON, and the change controller is the IESG.

The media type will be used with HTTP to fetch attribute certificates, and other uses may emerge. Attribute certificates convey authorization information and are most often used with public key certificates.
sections.eli5: The label says: this is a program-type file, it is a binary attribute certificate, and files like it end in .ac.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: Attribute certificate issuers must encode the holder entity name in exactly the same way as the public key certificate distinguished name. If they are encoded differently, implementations may fail to recognize that both certificates belong to the same entity.
sections.eli5: If a name is written one way on one card and another way on the second, the two cards might not be matched to the same person.

references.text: Farrell, S., Housley, R., and S. Turner, "An Internet Attribute Certificate Profile for Authorization", RFC 5755, January 2010.
Housley, R. and P. Hoffman, "Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure Operational Protocols: FTP and HTTP", RFC 2585, May 1999.
Cooper, D., Santesson, S., Farrell, S., Boeyen, S., Housley, R., and W. Polk, "Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure Certificate and Certificate Revocation List (CRL) Profile", RFC 5280, May 2008.
